Writing note: GPT-6 generated this article from my conversations and hands-on work with Codex. It looks back at the first Andy Live task: moving photos from the camera to a website. That pipeline now works; admin review, customer QR codes, and payments have not yet been deployed.

My initial goal sounded simple: take a photo on location and let the client see it on a website a little later. Once I started, I realized that “from shutter to website” was a chain of handoffs. The camera had to pass a file to my phone, the phone to cloud storage, and the website had to know what to show. Then I had to decide who could download or remove each photo.

This account follows the order in which Codex and I actually worked through the problems. The configuration screenshot contains no credentials or customer photos, and the error messages retain only what is useful for troubleshooting. At the time of writing, photo transfer and the live gallery are online. Code for admin review, customer QR codes, and Stripe payments has passed local checks in a separate repository, but it is not configured or deployed to the production site.

Start with one 2MP photo

At first, I considered high-resolution USB import, face recognition, automatic editing, and online sales. But the easiest file to get reliably from the Nikon D5600 to my phone was the roughly 2MP copy transferred by SnapBridge. I had no similarly convenient way to transfer the full-resolution original automatically. So the first version focused on one route:

D5600 → SnapBridge → Android phone → FolderSync → Cloudflare R2 → /live page

This is not fully unattended. I sometimes still have to tap once to move a photo from the D5600 to the phone. FolderSync handles the scheduled upload after that. Keeping those steps distinct matters: when a new photo is missing from the page, I need to know whether it is stuck at the camera, phone, cloud, or website.

Phone to R2: filling the form was only the first hurdle

I created a private Cloudflare R2 bucket named andy-live. At that point it was empty:

FolderSync lists S3 Compatible under file protocols, not among the cloud services above it. After finding it, I still had to map Cloudflare’s credential names to the fields on my phone:

FolderSync fieldR2 value
Access Key IDR2 access key ID
Secret Access KeyR2 secret access key
Server addresshttps://<Account ID>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com
Regionauto

The token value is not the S3 Access Key ID, and the server address is not the bucket page URL. The account test first returned Access Denied. It later gave a more specific error: us-west-2 was not a valid region, and the allowed values included auto. After setting auto and checking the token permissions, endpoint, and bucket scope, the account test passed.

Passing that test only proved the phone could connect to R2. It did not mean photos were syncing. I still had to create a folder pair: on the left, the phone directory where SnapBridge actually saved photos; on the right, the new S3 Compatible account and bucket. The direction was phone to cloud. I chose the shortest scheduled repeat interval, five minutes, and left experimental file encryption off.

Next came SyncFailedException. The useful clue was the on-screen “permission to access files not found” message, not the long Java stack trace. Android already allowed access to photos and videos, but FolderSync still needed the separate “manage all files” permission. Once that was granted, a photo finally reached R2. The first object path I saw was previews/_DSC0047.JPG.

Later, sync reported STREAMING-AWS4-HMAC-SHA256-PAYLOAD not implemented. I adjusted FolderSync’s quick remote-change check and its “disable checksum calculation” option, and the error stopped. Both settings changed during the same troubleshooting round, so I cannot attribute the fix confidently to just one. I can say that this combination uploaded successfully from my phone to R2.

Objects in R2 made the website useful

Once photos appeared in the bucket, the next question was how R2 would reach my website. We built a separate service for andy-live. The server uses read-only credentials to list R2 objects and create short-lived access links; the bucket remains private. The live page groups photos into 20-minute intervals using their upload times and polls for updates after the phone syncs.

I did not want the page restricted to “the latest 50 photos.” Once we added a review mechanism, the better rule became clear: show every photo that I have reviewed and explicitly made public, rather than exposing every new object in the bucket. Sync and page polling also generate R2 requests, so actual operation counts matter alongside storage capacity.

Two promises needed care. First, the time shown on the page comes from an R2 object’s upload or modification time, not the camera’s shutter time. Second, adding “please save your photos promptly” to a page is easy. Promising deletion within 24 hours requires a real cleanup job and a retention rule for purchased files. A line of copy cannot enforce a deadline the system has not implemented.

Once photos were visible, who could see and receive them?

With the live page working, I started asking whether every uploaded photo should be public. If someone bought one photo, how could I stop them from downloading a whole batch? Could I immediately take down a problematic image from my phone?

At that point, andy-live grew from an object-list page into a small access-control system. New uploads should wait for my review. From a mobile admin page I can select photos, and the system can prepare watermarked viewing copies and separate 2MP delivery files. The public gallery, a customer’s QR-code page, and the post-payment download link each have different permissions:

A customer QR code contains only the photos I select and can expire or be revoked. Payment is per photo. A return from Stripe’s checkout page is not enough to permit a download: the server must receive and verify the payment webhook, then match the share link, photo, and order. The admin interface can also unpublish or delete photos and inspect recent orders. For now, the delivery file is still the roughly 2MP straight-out-of-camera copy transferred by SnapBridge, not a full-resolution original that has yet to enter R2.

I also kept asking whether HK$10 per photo made sense after payment fees, and what business or venue rules applied to small-scale street photography. Stripe does not settle those questions. Automatic payment can establish an order’s payment state; pricing, operating arrangements, and compliance need separate decisions before real sales begin.

I also needed to know where website changes came from

While adding the 20-minute grouping, I asked a seemingly mundane question: “Which copy of the code on the server did we actually change?” If the only change lived in a manual server edit, how would I reproduce or roll it back?

We later separated andy-live into its own private GitHub repository and connected GitHub Actions. Changes are checked locally; pull requests run automated tests. After a merge to the main branch, the pipeline builds an image. The Contabo server starts a candidate container and checks the page, health endpoint, and photo endpoint before replacing the live container. I can now identify which commit is running instead of relying on my memory of a past server edit.

That also explains why the second version is not live yet. Code for admin review, QR codes, per-photo payments, and configurable cleanup has been written. Fifteen local tests, including tests with a temporary PostgreSQL database, plus type checks and a build have passed. Production still needs an admin R2 write credential, a database and login configuration, a Stripe merchant account, and test payment webhooks. Automatic cleanup is disabled by default, so I cannot claim that the production site already deletes photos on a schedule.

What works now

As of October 3, 2026, the work falls into two groups:

Working nowStill needs configuration and end-to-end checks
D5600 to phone through SnapBridge, with a manual tap when neededAdmin R2 read/write credentials and database
FolderSync uploads roughly 2MP photos to private R2Production checks for admin login, review, and QR codes
/live displays photos in 20-minute groupsStripe test payments, webhooks, per-photo downloads, and refunds
Independent-repository CI/CD and candidate-container checksBackup and restore rehearsal, final retention rules, and rollout

Looking back, the project advanced when I kept asking one question: “Where has the file reached?” After an account test passes, check whether an object exists. After an object exists, check whether the page can read it. Only then address review and sales. Each handoff leaves observable evidence, which tells me where to begin the next investigation.

写作说明：本文由 GPT-6 生成，整理自我与 Codex 的讨论和实际操作，回顾 Andy Live 第一版从相机传图到网页的任务。第一版链路已经跑通；后台审核、客户二维码和收款功能仍待部署。

我最初想做的事情很简单：在现场拍完照，让对方过一会儿就能从网页看到照片。真正动手后，我才发现“拍完就上网”不是一个动作，而是一连串交接。相机要把文件交给手机，手机要交给云存储，网站要知道该展示什么，最后还得想清楚谁能下载、谁能删除。

这篇文章按我和 CodeX 实际解决问题的顺序写。文中的配置截图没有密钥，也没有客人的照片；报错信息保留了排障所需的部分。写到这里时，传图和现场展示已经上线，后台审核、客户二维码与 Stripe 收款的代码已在独立仓库完成本地验证，尚未配置并部署到正式网站。

先把目标缩到一张 2MP 照片

一开始，我也想过高清 USB 抽图、人脸识别、自动修图和在线售卖。但尼康 D5600 到手机这一步，最容易稳定取得的是 SnapBridge 传来的约 2MP 照片。高清原图没有同样省事的自动传输方式。于是第一版先不碰这些能力，只验证：

D5600 → SnapBridge → Android 手机 → FolderSync → Cloudflare R2 → /live 网页

这不是完全无人值守。D5600 到手机有时仍要我手动点一下；手机之后才由 FolderSync 按计划同步。把这点讲清楚很重要，否则网页上没有新照片时，我会把相机、手机、云端和网站混成同一个故障。

手机到 R2：表单填对只是第一关

我先在 Cloudflare 创建了私有存储桶 andy-live。那时桶里还是空的：

FolderSync 的账户类型藏在“文件协议”下的 S3 Compatible，不在上面的云服务列表里。找到它之后，Cloudflare 给我的几项凭据又和手机上的字段名称不完全一致。最后我把对应关系整理成这样：

FolderSync 字段R2 对应内容
Access Key IDR2 的访问密钥 ID
Secret Access KeyR2 的机密访问密钥
服务器地址https://<Account ID>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com
区域auto

令牌值不是 S3 的 Access Key ID；服务器地址也不是存储桶页面的网址。手机账号测试一开始报 Access Denied，随后又明确提示 us-west-2 不是有效区域，列出的可用值包含 auto。改用 auto 并核对令牌权限、地址和存储桶范围后，账户测试终于通过。

然而“账户测试通过”只证明手机能连接 R2，不代表照片已经在同步。我还得建文件夹配对：左侧选手机里 SnapBridge 实际保存照片的目录，右侧选刚才建立的 S3 Compatible 账户与存储桶，方向选从手机到云端。计划任务用五分钟作为最短重复间隔，文件加密先不启用。

接下来又遇到一次 SyncFailedException。真正有用的线索是界面上的“未找到访问文件的权限”，不是那一长串 Java 堆栈。Android 的“照片和视频”权限已经允许，但 FolderSync 仍缺少“管理所有文件”的访问权；补齐后，照片才真正进入 R2。我第一次在对象列表里看到的路径是 previews/_DSC0047.JPG。

之后同步还报过 STREAMING-AWS4-HMAC-SHA256-PAYLOAD not implemented。我调整了 FolderSync 的远端快速检查和“禁用校验和计算”选项，错误停止了。因为两个选项是在同一轮排查中调整的，我不能把结果武断地归因于其中某一个；可以确认的是，这组设置在当时的手机与 R2 组合上完成了上传。

R2 有了对象，网页才开始有意义

照片进桶以后，下一问才是“R2 怎么到我的网站”。我们给 andy-live 做了独立的网页服务，由服务器用只读凭据列出 R2 对象并生成短时访问链接；存储桶本身继续保持私有。现场页按上传时间每 20 分钟分一组，手机同步后，页面会轮询更新。

我当时不想把现场页限制成“只显示最新 50 张”。后来补上审核机制，这个想法有了更准确的边界：可以展示全部已审核且明确设为公开的照片，而不是把桶里每个刚上传的文件都直接放出来。同步频率和页面轮询也会增加 R2 请求数，所以还要看实际操作量，不能只盯着存储容量。

这里有两个容易说过头的地方。第一，网页显示的时间来自 R2 对象的上传或修改时间，并不是相机快门的拍摄时间。第二，页面上写“请及时保存”很容易，真正承诺“24 小时内删除”却必须有实际清理任务与付款后的保留规则。没有做到的期限，不能只靠一行提示文字来保证。

当照片能看见，问题变成“谁可以看、谁可以拿”

看到现场页正常工作后，我开始担心另一件事：所有传上来的照片是不是都该公开？如果客户只买一张，能否阻止他把整批照片下载走？万一某张照片有问题，我能不能在手机上立刻撤下？

这时 andy-live 从“对象列表页面”变成了一个带权限的小系统。我们决定让新上传的照片先处于待审核状态；我在手机后台选图，系统再生成带水印的浏览图，以及独立存放的 2MP 交付文件。公开现场页、客户二维码页与付款后的下载地址各有不同权限：

客户二维码只包含我挑选的照片，可以设置有效期或撤销。付款按照片逐张计算，不能靠客户从 Stripe 付款页面“返回成功”就放行下载；服务器必须收到并核验付款回调，再核对分享链接、照片和订单。后台还能下架或删除照片，查看最近订单状态。现在交付文件仍是 SnapBridge 得到的约 2MP 直出图，不是尚未接入的相机高清原图。

在技术之外，我也反复问过：一张卖 HK$10 是否值得，支付手续费会吃掉多少，小规模街头拍摄又涉及哪些经营与场地规则。这些问题没有因为接入 Stripe 就消失。自动收款只能处理付款状态；定价、经营安排和合规判断仍要在真正营业前单独确认。

改网页，也得知道代码从哪里来

在我们给现场页加时间分组时，我又追问了一个看似琐碎的问题：“这页到底改的是服务器上的哪一份代码？”如果只在服务器里手工改，下一次怎么复现、怎么回滚？

后来我们把 andy-live 拆成独立的私有 GitHub 仓库，给它接上 GitHub Actions。代码先在本地检查，PR 再跑自动测试；合并到主分支后构建镜像，由 Contabo 服务器先启动候选容器，检查页面、健康接口和照片接口，成功才替换正式容器。这样，网站正在运行哪个提交，终于可以核对，而不必凭“我记得当时改过”来判断。

这也解释了为什么现在的第二版还没有直接上线。后台、二维码、逐张收款和可配置清理已经写好，15 项本地测试（含临时 PostgreSQL）、类型检查与构建通过；但正式服务器还缺后台专用 R2 写入凭据、数据库与登录配置，Stripe 商家账户和测试回调也尚未接通。自动清理默认关闭，不能宣称线上已经在定时删照片。

目前跑通了什么

截至 2026 年 10 月 3 日，可以把整个过程分成两段：

已经可用仍待配置和联通测试
D5600 经 SnapBridge 到手机；必要时手动确认后台专用 R2 读写凭据与数据库
FolderSync 把约 2MP 照片送进私有 R2管理员登录、审核、二维码的正式环境验证
/live 展示照片并按 20 分钟分组Stripe 测试付款、回调、逐张下载与退款流程
独立仓库的 CI/CD 与服务器候选镜像检查备份恢复演练、清理期限的最终选择与上线

回看这些对话，真正推进项目的，不是一次性把所有功能列齐，而是每次只问“文件现在到了哪里”。账户测试通过后要看对象有没有出现；对象出现后要看网页是否能读；网页能读后才谈审核和售卖。每一段都留下可观察的结果，也就知道下一次出问题该从哪一段查起。

entry.content:
It has been more than a year since I uploaded my first blog post.

Over the past year, continually using various AI tools has given me a firsthand sense of what “changing with each passing day” really means.

Take the process of updating a blog post as an example.

At the beginning, I had to create a new Markdown file in the project myself, link the images in code, and then run Hexo’s deployment and rendering commands before I could publish the article to the server.

At that point, the data flow was rough and primitive:

my brain → project code → server

Later, I learned about CMSs (Content Management Systems).

With CodeX’s help, I added a content-management page to my blog and even went so far as to add skins for different universities.

I also connected a DeepSeek API, which could help me translate content directly into English.

The data flow then became:

my brain → CMS frontend → project code → server

But now my way of providing input has been simplified once again.

After editing an article in Obsidian, I can simply ask CodeX to read it, translate it, and merge it into the codebase. One sentence is enough to complete the process.

The data flow is now:

my brain → Obsidian → CodeX → project code → server

To me, this process feels like a series of layers of abstraction. I have moved from touching the raw code directly, to wrapping it in a frontend page, and now to skipping the frontend altogether while an agent enters the raw content for me.

Each of the three methods has its own advantages:

  • The first method lets me interact with the details of the code, like opening an electrical box and operating it from inside.
  • The second is more Web 2.0: frontend and backend are separated, and the mode of human-computer activity is more pleasant.
  • The third feels like having a servant. I no longer need to care about execution; I only need to pass the request to someone else.

In my view, an Agent/Harness is like an operating system for a large language model. It constrains the model so that its intelligence can be applied in the right direction. I wonder what it will become in the future.

It is rather strange that this website, with its Web 1.0 visual style, uses the most advanced large-model technology to discuss content from different eras—swallowing everything whole without fully digesting it.

entry.content:
自从第一篇博客内容上传完成到现在，已经一年有余。

在这一年里不断地使用各种Ai工具，让我切身体会到了什么叫做“日新月异”。

以我更新一篇文章为例：

在最开始的时候，我需要自己在项目里新建md文件，同时用代码链接好图片，接着执行Hexo的部署和渲染命令，然后实现我的文章部署到服务器。

这个时候的数据流向很粗糙原始：我的大脑-工程代码-服务器

后面我了解到了CMS（Content Management System）内容管理系统。

于是我在CodeX的帮助下，给我的博客增加了一套内容管理系统的页面，甚至煞有介事地增加了各个学校的皮肤。

同时我接入了Deepseek的API，可以帮助我直接把内容翻译成英文。

这个时候的数据流向就是：我的大脑-CMS前端-工程代码-服务器。

而到了现在，我的输入方式又一次简化了。

我在Obsidian里面编辑好了之后，直接让CodeX去阅读，并且把文章翻译完成，并入到代码里，可以说一句话就完成了。

数据流向是：我的大脑-Obsidian-CodeX-工程代码-服务器

在我看来，这个过程就像是一层层封装一样，从我直接接触原始代码，到封装一层前端页面，再到现在的直接跳过前端，Agent操作原始内容直接录入。

三种方法都有各自的好处：

  • 第一种方法让我可以接触到代码细节，就像是拆开电箱在里面直接操作
  • 第二种方法更加Web2.0，前后端分离，人机活动模式更加宜人
  • 第三种方式就像是多了一个仆人，我不再需要关注执行，只需要把要求丢给其他人做

在我看来Agent/Harness就像是大模型的操作系统，给模型约束，让它能够在正确地方向上发挥自己的智能，不知道未来又会变成什么样子。

非常怪异地，我这个画风如Web1.0的网站，用最先进的大模型的技术，讨论着不同时代的内容，囫囵吞枣，把所有的东西吃下去。

entry.content:
While studying in Hong Kong, I do not know whether it was excessive stress or an air-conditioning unit that was too loud, but my sleep was affected. On top of that, I drank a cup of milk tea after every meal during my internship, and my weight climbed above 82 kg.

After the internship ended, all the data for my thesis had been collected. I was reading papers, writing the thesis, and preparing for my defense at the same time.

At that point, I felt that I absolutely could not go into the defense in that condition.

On the one hand, since my thesis was about fitness, I felt that I should at least produce some results as the author of the thesis. On the other hand, this might be the last time in my life that I would be studying at a school. I wanted the person in the photos to look at least somewhat healthy, so that years later I would remember myself as spirited rather than in terrible physical condition.

So I started controlling my diet while swimming and working out. Every day, I traveled between home, the gym, the swimming pool, and the library.

You can find the record of my swimming-related article here.

Training log
01 / 04

Of course, I think the most important part is diet control.

Metabolic calculations

Resting metabolic rate (RMR)

The Mifflin–St Jeor equation can be used to calculate resting metabolic rate—the calories your body burns just by being alive and breathing.

For men:

$$
RMR=10W+6.25H-5A+5
$$

For women:

$$
RMR=10W+6.25H-5A-161
$$

RMR stands for Resting Metabolic Rate.
Here, W is measured in kilograms, H in centimeters, and A is age.

For example, the RMR of an 80 kg, 177 cm, 25-year-old man is:

$$
10\times80+6.25\times177-5\times25+5=1786.25\ \mathrm{kcal}
$$

Note: kcal is a unit of energy, or kilocalorie. Converted to the international unit joule:

$$
1\ \mathrm{kcal}=4.184\ \mathrm{kJ}
$$

In other words, this man would burn about that many calories per day simply by staying alive and breathing. Of course, the equation is not precise; it is only a rough estimate.

Total daily energy expenditure (TDEE)

TDEE stands for Total Daily Energy Expenditure.

$$
\mathrm{TDEE}=\mathrm{RMR}+\text{daily activity}+\text{exercise}+\text{thermic effect of food}
$$

A simple conversion from RMR to TDEE can be expressed as:

$$
\mathrm{TDEE}=\mathrm{RMR}\times\text{Activity Factor}
$$

Activity levelFactor
Sedentary, little to no exercise1.20
Light activity, exercise 1–3 times per week1.375
Moderate activity, exercise 3–5 times per week1.55
High activity, exercise 6–7 times per week1.725
Very high activity / physically demanding work1.90

For example, the 80 kg, 177 cm, 25-year-old man above has a moderate activity level:

$$
\mathrm{TDEE}=1770\times1.55=2744\ \mathrm{kcal/day}
$$

If you want to lose fat, your daily calorie intake must be lower than your TDEE.
If you want to gain weight, your daily calorie intake must be higher than your TDEE.

The macronutrients that provide energy include:

  • Carbohydrates: $4\ \mathrm{kcal/g}$
  • Fat: $9\ \mathrm{kcal/g}$
  • Protein: $4\ \mathrm{kcal/g}$

For fat loss, the main target is body fat. Because human adipose tissue is not pure fat—it also contains water, cellular structures, and other components—a common estimate is:

$$
1\ \mathrm{kg}\ \text{of body fat}\approx7{,}700\ \mathrm{kcal}
$$

Therefore, if the daily calorie deficit—the TDEE minus calorie intake—is 500 kcal, it would take about 15.4 days to lose 1 kg of body fat.

At the same time, food intake is also affected by digestion, metabolic efficiency, and other factors, such as mood and hormones.

Making sure that you do not have metabolic problems, avoiding hormone medication, staying in a good mood, sleeping well, and drinking enough water are also very important.

Diet log

My original diet plan was based on a Zhihu blogger’s approach. The goal was convenience, clean eating, and sufficient simplicity.

As the image shows, the nutrients in the plan came from:

  • Carbohydrates: apples, citrus, pears, oats, and tomatoes
  • Fat: egg yolks and milk
  • Protein: chicken breast, egg whites, and milk
  • Dietary fiber: cucumbers, apples, pears, and tomatoes
  • Vitamins: tomatoes

There were also various trace elements and amino acids. Since the ingredients were all whole foods and did not require additional cooking techniques, calculating the nutritional intake was fairly simple.

Written record

The Evolution of Psychology argues that although Homo sapiens have entered modern life, our genes are not very different from those of the hunter-gatherers of ancient times.

The diet of early humans may have alternated between feasting and fasting, without the need for a fixed eating routine, while still relying mainly on carbohydrates. I therefore tried an experiment on myself based on the daily intake described above: I prepared the food in advance, or each morning, and then finished eating all of it at different times throughout the day.

Diet experiment
01 / 04

The relatively stable diet plan I eventually developed was:

  • Prepare the ingredients in advance: cucumbers, apples, citrus, cubed chicken breast, washed lettuce, and eggs.
  • Buy an enormous rice cooker. In the morning, put all the ingredients into it, add water and salt depending on my mood, and boil everything for an hour.
  • After an hour of morning exercise, return home, drain the water, place the ingredients in a food-grade stainless-steel basin, portion them out, and finish them all in one day.

Apart from being unpleasant to eat, it was a fairly efficient diet plan.

Later, however, I felt that it was too inefficient and tasted too bad. My current plan is:

  • Cook several kilograms of brown rice at once each week, portion it, and freeze it.
  • Prepare chicken breast, chicken legs, chicken wings, and beef in an air fryer in one batch, then refrigerate them.
  • When eating, put everything together and heat it in the microwave. The whole meal takes less than ten minutes.

Conclusion

I first encountered fitness during my undergraduate years. I went on to train systematically, read professional books on nutrition and kinesiology, watch professional fitness videos, train at the gym, and eventually explore street workout. It has been almost ten years, with intermittent periods of being lean, overweight, bulky, and muscular. Looking back on these different phases, I can be certain that my physical condition—the material foundation—has influenced my mental state, and vice versa, to a considerable extent.

In the preface of my master’s thesis, I quoted Mark Rippetoe, the author of Basic Barbell Training:

“Physical strength is the most important thing in life. Although its importance to daily life has declined throughout human history, its importance to life itself has never diminished… The strong body formed through millions of years of human evolution will not disappear simply because the desk was invented.”

I also wrote in my own preface:

“A strong body not only gives a person greater control over themselves and their environment on a physical level, but also makes them more confident psychologically. This is highly beneficial to a person’s growth and development.”

When I had just started studying at HKU, I felt that my mental and physical condition was at the lowest point of my life. I once felt that I had nothing left.

But I signed up for a one-on-one leg mobility competition at the university sports center, and I could still take first place on the leaderboard in random matches against people I had never met. In a Muay Thai class, I could still immediately learn material that was completely unfamiliar to me, and I was selected as a demonstration student to spar with the coach.

So I knew that even if I had forgotten or lost many kinds of knowledge and abilities, the muscles and cells in my body had never betrayed me. I could still win. I think that is the most important thing fitness has given me.

This article records some of my explorations and experiences with fitness and diet. I hope it can also help anyone who needs it.

在香港读书期间不知是压力过大还是窗机太吵，睡眠收到了影响，加上实习工作期间每天饭后一杯科技奶茶，体重飙到了82KG+

实习结束之后回到家里，毕业论文全部的数据都已经搜集完毕，一边读文献、写论文，准备答辩。

那个时候觉得，绝对不能以这样的状态去答辩。

一方面我觉得，既然我的毕业论文做的是健身有关的内容，至少我作为论文的作者，得拿出一些成果吧？
再一方面，我觉得，这次答辩很可能是我人生最后在学校读书的时候了，我希望照片里的我至少状态可以好一些，等到多年以后我会想起来的是意气风发，而不是身体状态非常糟糕。

所以饮食调控和游泳健身同步开始，每天在家-健身房-游泳池-图书馆往返。
关于游泳的文章记录可见游泳文章记录

训练记录
01 / 04

当然我觉得最值得注意的是饮食控制这一部分。

代谢计算

静息代谢RMR

根据Mifflin–St Jeor 的公式计算静息代谢（什么都不干，呼吸就会消耗的热量）

男性：

$$
RMR=10W+6.25H-5A+5
$$

女性：

$$
RMR=10W+6.25H-5A-161
$$

Resting Metabolic Rate，静息代谢率
其中 W 是 kg，H 是 cm，A 是年龄
例子：80kg，177cm，25岁男性的RMR =

$$
10\times80+6.25\times177-5\times25+5=1786.25\ \mathrm{kcal}
$$

注：kcal是能量单位千卡，换算成国际单位焦耳是

$$
1\ \mathrm{kcal}=4.184\ \mathrm{kJ}
$$

即该男子每天只要是活着进行呼吸作用就需要消耗这么多热量，当然这个计算公式并不够精确，只是一个粗糙的值

每日总能量消耗TDEE

TDEE是Total Daily Energy Expenditure的缩写。

$$
\mathrm{TDEE}=\mathrm{RMR}+\text{日常活动}+\text{运动}+\text{食物热效应}
$$

TDEE和RMR的一个简单换算公式可以用以下公式来表示：

$$
\mathrm{TDEE}=\mathrm{RMR}\times\text{Activity Factor}
$$

活动水平系数
久坐，几乎不运动1.20
轻度活动，每周运动 1–3 次1.375
中度活动，每周运动 3–5 次1.55
高度活动，每周运动 6–7 次1.725
极高活动 / 重体力劳动1.90
例如，上述80kg，177cm，25岁男性，每天中度活动。

$$
\mathrm{TDEE}=1770\times1.55=2744\ \mathrm{kcal/day}
$$

如果需要减脂，那么就要确保每日摄入的热量低于TDEE
如果需要增重，那么就要确保每日摄入的热量高于TDEE

能提供热量的营养物质包括：

  • 碳水化合物：$4\ \mathrm{kcal/g}$
  • 脂肪：$9\ \mathrm{kcal/g}$
  • 蛋白质：$4\ \mathrm{kcal/g}$

而对于减脂来说，主要是减去体脂，由于人体脂肪组织不全是纯脂肪，还包含水分、细胞结构等，一般经验认为：

$$
1\ \mathrm{kg}\ \text{体脂}\approx7{,}700\ \mathrm{kcal}
$$

所以如果每天的热量缺口（TDEE减去摄入）为500kcal的话，减去1kg体脂的时间大约需要15.4天

同时，由于食物摄入后还受到消化、代谢效率等因素等影响（情绪影响消化、体内激素影响代谢效率）

确保自己没有代谢问题、没有服用激素药物、保持好心情、睡眠和足够的饮水也是非常重要的。

饮食记录

最初我的饮食计划是按照一个知乎博主的文章方案来的，目标就是方便+干净，以及足够简单。

从图片里面可以看出，摄入的营养成分包括：

  • 碳水化合物：苹果、柑橘、梨、燕麦、番茄
  • 脂肪：鸡蛋黄、牛奶
  • 蛋白质：鸡胸肉、鸡蛋白、牛奶
  • 膳食纤维：黄瓜、苹果、梨、番茄
  • 维生素：番茄
    以及各种微量元素和氨基酸等，由于都是纯物质，也没有额外的烹饪手法，所以计算营养摄入也很简单。

文字记录

《进化心理学》认为，智人虽然进入了现代化的生活，但是实际上基因层面上，和远古时期依靠狩猎的原始人并没有多大的区别。

原始人的饮食方式可能是饥一顿饱一顿，不需要保持固定的饮食习惯，不过依然以碳水为主。
因此，我尝试按照上述的每日摄入情况，对自己的饮食进行了人体实验，具体就是提前或者每天早上准备好，接着在一天不同的时间段把这些食物全部吃完。

饮食实验
01 / 04

最后在当时形成的一套比较稳定的饮食方案是：

  • 提前准备好食材（黄瓜、苹果、柑橘、鸡胸肉切块、生菜洗好、鸡蛋）
  • 买一个巨大无比的电饭煲，早上把所有的食材丢到电饭煲里，看心情加水和盐、煮一小时
  • 晨练1小时后回家，把水倒掉，把食材放入食品级不锈钢盆里，分装好，一天吃完

除了难吃之外，算是一个比较高效的饮食方案了。

不过后面还是觉得效率太低，和口感太差目前最新的方案是：

  • 每周把糙米饭一次性煮若干公斤，分装好放到冷冻
  • 把鸡胸肉/鸡腿肉/鸡翅/牛肉一次性用空气炸锅制备好放入冷藏
  • 每天摄入的时候放在一起，用微波炉加热，10分钟内摄入完毕。

结语

关于健身，从我本科开始接触，再到我开始系统训练和阅读专业的营养学、运动学书籍，看专业健身视频自己去健身房训练，再到开始接触街头健身。至今已经有快10年，中间断断续续地经历了纤细、肥胖、臃肿、健硕各种不同的身材。回顾这些不同的时候，我可以确信的是我的身体状态（物质基础）确实很大程度上和我的精神状况互相影响（思维和存在）

翻开我的硕士毕业论文，我引用了Basic Barbell Training的作者马克里皮托在前言里的话——

“体力是生命中最重要的东西，虽然随着人类历史的发展，体力对日常生活的重要性越来越低，但它对生命的重要性却从未降低……，我们经过几百万年进化形成的强壮身体不会因为办公桌的发明而消失。“

以及我在前言里写的
*“强健的身体不仅能让个人在身体层面上对自己和环境有更强的控制力，还能让一个人在心理上更加自信，这对一个人的成长和发展都是非常有益的”

在我刚刚到港大读书的时候，我的身心状况在我自己看来，处于我人生的低谷，我曾经觉得我已一无所有。

但是我报名参加了学校体育中心的一对一腿部灵活度比赛，我还是可以在随机的路人对抗里在排行榜拿下第一；在泰拳课上我依然能够马上学会我完全不懂的内容，被选为演示学员和教练对打。

所以我知道，哪怕很多知识和能力，我忘记了，我失去了，但是我身体里的肌肉和细胞从未背叛我，我依然可以赢，我觉得这就是健身所带给我的最重要的东西。

此文介绍了我在健身和饮食上的一些探索和经历，作为记录，也希望可以帮到有需要的人。

entry.content:
在若干年前的一段时间，我曾经感觉到我的人生停滞了，日复一日的过一样的日子。

在本科的四年里，我强迫自己不待在宿舍里玩英雄联盟，每天待的最多的地方是教室和图书馆，还有唯一开到12点的文科楼的自习室，因为除了要完成我不喜欢的化学课的作业以外，我还要自学其他科的内容。

可能也是这样的原因，我大学四年没有玩的电子游戏，在那段时间全部玩了。

那是一款跑酷竞速类的游戏，玩家控制游戏角色，可以实现前后左右还有跳跃、冲刺，利用各种地图中的道具到达终点。

在高考之后我就已经厌恶了竞争，或者说，我并不喜欢无意义的竞争，那些不在知识的广度上增加，只是为了让自己更加熟练于某个题目不扣分的竞争我尤其不喜欢。

对于这款游戏来说，既然是竞速比赛，那就必然有名次，结果还是回到了竞争，而且地图只有这么一个，如果想要获得前列的名次，还是得一次又一次地重复，总结经验，最后才能拿下冠军。

其中有一个地图叫做“逃离地狱”，港服的名称叫做“绝不回头”。

地图设定在猩红色的背景里，玩家只能看到眼前不到几米的路，而这条路也只有大约3人宽，如果掉下去，就得回到原地重新开始。

金杯（即表示在限定时间内跑完这个地图，挑战成功后会获取一个金杯标识，代表精通）的标准是在48秒内跑完全程。

但是我第一次跑了3小时。

我尝试过慢慢地走，发现到了后半段路开始有缺口，需要配合跳跃和冲刺；后面我开始正常速度跑，发现在最后一段还会出现骷髅虚影，如果被撞到，就会被弹开，掉入虚空，回到开头，重头再来。

就这样一次又一次地重复重复重复，我已经忘记重复了多少次了。

不过我慢慢的开始了解到，整个赛道的路线大致如何，了解到什么地方会有坑，什么地方应该按照什么固定的模式来跑。

直到最后，我也能够像别人发出来的视频里那样，全程最高速度，如入无人之境地拿下金杯。

诀窍就是不断地重复、试错、不要担心从头再来，在一次次的重复中不断理解全局，而在这个地图上花的时间，加起来也不过五到六个小时而已。

在我过去的人生里，好像也是这样，如履薄冰又加速向前，巨大的突破和变化，似乎都是我独自训练的时候实现的。

“逃离地狱”和“绝不回头”，是内地服务器和香港服务器的不同翻译。相比之下我更喜欢后者——前者表示的是逃离不喜欢的环境，后者我认为是表示一往无前的决心。

《游褒禅山记》里说，“至于幽暗昏惑而无物以相知”这样的情形常常在我的生活里出现，这个时候没有任何人可以给我清晰的答案。

这样的时候我总是告诉自己：“勇往直前，绝不回头”。

黄色的树林中岔开两条路，
可惜我不能同时踏足，
我一介旅人，久久伫立着
沿着其中一条路极目望去，
直到它拐弯没入灌丛。

随后我选择另一条路，它同样可行，
或许更值得选择，
因为它荒草萋萋，盼人涉足，
尽管说到底，这两条路
被来往的脚步磨得相差无几。

那天清晨，两条路静卧着，
覆满落叶，未被足迹踏黑，
哦，我把第一条路留待他日再走！
可我深知，此路连着彼路，
恐怕我将不会再折返。

很久很久以后，在某处地方
我叹息着讲起此事：
树林中岔开两条路，而我——
我选择了那条少有人走的路，
所有的一切皆因此而变得不同。

《未选择的路》——罗伯特·弗罗斯特

entry.content:
A few years ago, I felt that my life had come to a standstill. I was living the same day over and over again.

During my four years as an undergraduate, I forced myself not to stay in my dormitory playing League of Legends. I spent most of my time in classrooms and libraries, as well as in the liberal arts building’s self-study room, the only one that stayed open until midnight. Besides completing assignments for chemistry classes I did not enjoy, I also had to teach myself other subjects.

Perhaps for the same reason, I played all the video games I had not played during those four years of university during that period instead.

It was a parkour racing game. Players controlled a character who could move in all directions, jump, dash, and use items scattered across each map to reach the finish line.

After the gaokao, I had already grown tired of competition—or perhaps I simply did not like meaningless competition. I especially disliked competing in ways that did not expand the breadth of my knowledge, but only made me more practiced at avoiding mistakes on a particular question.

For this game, however, a race naturally meant rankings. I was back in competition, and there was only one map. If I wanted to place near the top, I still had to repeat the map again and again, summarize what I had learned, and eventually win the championship.

One of the maps was called “Escape from Hell.” On the Hong Kong server, its name was “Never Look Back.”

The map was set against a scarlet background. Players could see less than a few meters of the path ahead, and the path was only about three people wide. If you fell, you had to return to the starting point and begin again.

The standard for the gold cup—an indicator of mastery awarded for completing the map within the time limit—was to finish the entire course in 48 seconds.

But on my first attempt, I took three hours.

I tried walking slowly and discovered that gaps began to appear in the second half, requiring a combination of jumps and dashes. Later, I began running at a normal speed, only to find that ghostly skeletons appeared in the final section. If I collided with one, I would be knocked away, fall into the void, return to the beginning, and start all over again.

And so I repeated it, again and again and again. I have forgotten how many times I did it.

But little by little, I began to understand the general route of the track. I learned where the holes were and which fixed pattern I should follow in each section.

Eventually, I was able to run at full speed, just like in the videos other people had posted, and win the gold cup as if there were no obstacles at all.

The trick was to keep repeating, keep experimenting, and not be afraid of starting over. Through repetition, I gradually came to understand the whole picture. In total, I had spent only five or six hours on that map.

My life in the past seems to have been similar: walking on thin ice while accelerating forward. The biggest breakthroughs and changes often seemed to happen when I was training alone.

“Escape from Hell” and “Never Look Back” are different translations used by the mainland and Hong Kong servers. I prefer the latter. The former suggests escaping from an environment I dislike; the latter, to me, expresses a determination to move forward without turning back.

In A Record of the Stone Bell Mountain, Wang Anshi wrote of a situation “where darkness, confusion, and obscurity leave nothing by which one can understand it.” Circumstances like that often appear in my life, when no one can give me a clear answer.

At times like that, I always tell myself: “Move forward bravely. Never look back.”

Two roads diverged in a yellow wood,
And sorry I could not travel both,
Being one traveler, long I stood
And looked down one as far as I could
To where it bent in the undergrowth;

Then took the other, as just as fair,
And having perhaps the better claim,
Because it was grassy and wanted wear;
Though as for that the passing there
Had worn them really about the same,

And both that morning equally lay
In leaves no step had trodden black.
Oh, I kept the first for another day!
Yet knowing how way leads on to way,
I doubted if I should ever come back.

I shall be telling this with a sigh
Somewhere ages and ages hence:
Two roads diverged in a wood, and I—
I took the one less traveled by,
And that has made all the difference.

The Road Not Taken — Robert Frost

A PDF translation workflow made me rethink the data boundaries of cloud-based agents.

Translation note: This English version was translated by Codex (GPT-5) on 2026-09-19. The source text is the corresponding Chinese post in this repository.

Using Antigravity to Translate a PDF

In mid-September, I saw news coverage of an Anthropic threat report that contained a large number of disturbing cases (Anthropic, 2026b). I wanted to read the original report. When possible, I would rather consult a primary source than rely only on someone else’s summary.

I found the PDF on Anthropic’s website and downloaded it locally:

Detecting and countering misuse of AI: September 2026

I then asked Antigravity to process the PDF and translate it.

I used concurrent subtasks to improve speed. However, if the model is capable enough, these prompts may be unnecessary: the model may be able to decide which approach is most efficient by itself.

I also asked the Agent to make a simple count of the report’s different case categories:

About a year ago, I would not have expected an Agent itself to complete this kind of work. Now, many of the functional boundaries of specialized translation tools are being compressed by general-purpose Agents.

I had previously tried PDFMathTranslate. Its advantage is that it lets users choose different translation engines, but deployment and debugging are relatively cumbersome. These smaller capabilities can now also be implemented through a general-purpose Agent or a Codex sub-agent (PDFMathTranslate, n.d.).

Agents are flattening the “feature moats” of many specialized software products. In the future, the remaining moats may shift toward workflows, reliability, specialized data, compliance, user interfaces, and integrations.

After the Threat Report

The report quickly led to discussions about cybersecurity. It also described how intermediaries, proxies, and other infrastructure can expand the reach of model use (Anthropic, 2026b).

This reminded me that information security is not only a question of cryptography or server configuration.

The difference with an AI Agent is that its potential data access can be much broader than that of a traditional application. It does not merely wait for text input; it may also read files, call tools, execute commands, and send the results to a remote model for further processing.

How an Agent Works

In the cloud-based workflow I used, the model’s inference mainly happens in the cloud. For an Agent to process a local PDF, it must receive at least the relevant files or text. Exactly what gets uploaded depends on the client implementation, the Agent’s permissions, and the workflow.

When permissions, data boundaries, or the supply chain are poorly controlled, an Agent can shift from an “assistant” into a “thief”: it may read and upload data, and hand information that originally existed only on the local device to a third party.

On September 18, developer Ferstar reported through reverse engineering that a closed-source Agent from a Chinese foundation-model provider uploaded workspace snapshots. The provider later apologized and explained that the issue came from its repository indexing feature (Ferstar, 2026; IT之家, 2026).

The incident made me think that security boundaries cannot be evaluated only by asking whether a model trains on user data. We also need to ask: What did the client read? What did it upload? Who can decrypt it? How long is it stored? Can users actually disable the feature?

Possible Solutions

In June, Anthropic changed the data policy for Claude Fable. Fable now requires 30-day data retention by default for safety monitoring (Anthropic, 2026a). This change prompted some enterprise customers to question zero data retention (ZDR), intellectual property, and the scope of log retention.

Within days of the threat report’s publication on September 10, concerns from enterprise customers about AI data boundaries also became public. On September 14, Reuters, citing The Information, reported that NVIDIA, Palantir, Booz Allen, and other companies had begun restricting Anthropic models in sensitive workflows (Reuters, 2026).

Different solutions can be selected according to data sensitivity:

Ideally, all data could be processed locally and never leave the device. Even when a cloud provider offers compliance reviews and zero-data-retention guarantees, data that leaves the local device has entered a new trust boundary and cannot be treated as having the same security level as local processing.

The future will therefore likely focus on both safer, more efficient cloud computing and local models that are capable enough for demanding work.

One illustrative local AI setup for an individual or small team could be:

  1. Use Google Gemma 4 as the base model;
  2. Use NVIDIA DGX Spark as a small AI workstation.

This is only an illustrative combination. A real enterprise deployment would also need IAM, network isolation, auditing, key management, backups, and endpoint security.

Conclusion

What I really observed was not that Agents will necessarily “steal” data. It was that using a cloud-based Agent moves the security boundary beyond the local device and into the model provider, client, proxy service, plugins, and toolchain.

The more capable an Agent becomes, the more it can read and operate on. Least privilege, data classification, and verifiable supply-chain transparency will therefore become increasingly important.

Anthropic. (2026b, September 10). Detecting and countering misuse of AI: September 2026. https://www.anthropic.com/threat-intelligence-report-september-2026

一次 PDF 翻译实践，让我重新思考了云端 Agent 的数据边界。

使用 Antigravity 翻译 PDF

9 月中关注到新闻提到 Anthropic 的威胁报告，里面提到了大量震撼的内容（Anthropic, 2026b），于是便产生了阅读原文的想法。毕竟在条件允许的情况下，我还是更愿意直接阅读原始报告，而不是只依赖他人的二手总结。

我在 Anthropic 官网找到了报告的 PDF，然后下载到本地：

Detecting and countering misuse of AI: September 2026

接着给 Antigravity 下达命令，让它处理 PDF 翻译。

采用拆分并发的方式是为了提升速度。不过，如果模型本身的智能足够高，可能这些 Prompt 都是多余的，模型会自己判断什么样的方式最高效。

我还让 Agent 简单统计了一下威胁报告中不同类型案例的比例：

大约一年前，我还没有想过可以直接使用 Agent 本身的能力完成这一步骤。现在看来，很多垂直翻译工具的功能边界正在被通用 Agent 压缩。

之前我也尝试过 PDFMathTranslate。它的优点是可以自由选择不同的翻译引擎，但部署和调试相对繁琐；这些小功能现在也可以通过通用 Agent，或者 Codex 的子 Agent 来实现（PDFMathTranslate, n.d.）。

Agent 正在把很多垂直软件的“功能护城河”抹平。可能未来垂直软件真正剩下的护城河，会更多转向工作流、稳定性、专业数据、合规、UI 和集成。

威胁报告之后

威胁报告发布后，很快就出现了对网络安全的讨论。报告中提到了攻击者通过中间人、代理和其他基础设施扩大模型使用范围的问题（Anthropic, 2026b）。

这也让我再次意识到，“数据安全”并不是一个只和密码学或服务器配置有关的命题。

AI Agent 的不同之处在于，它获得的数据读取范围可能比传统应用大得多。它不只是等待用户输入文本，还可能读取文件、调用工具、执行命令，并把结果交给远程模型继续处理。

Agent 的工作原理

以这次使用的云端 Agent 为例，模型推理主要在云端完成。为了让 Agent 处理本地 PDF，它至少需要接收到任务相关的文件或文本；究竟上传哪些内容，则取决于客户端实现、Agent 权限和具体工作流。

当权限控制、数据边界或供应链存在问题时，Agent 可能从“助手”变成“小偷”：它有能力读取、上传，甚至把原本只存在于本地的数据交给第三方处理。

9 月 18 日，开发者 Ferstar 通过逆向分析指出，某国产大模型厂商的一款闭源 Agent 存在工作区快照上传行为；随后该厂商官方致歉，并解释称问题源于代码库索引功能（Ferstar, 2026; IT之家, 2026）。

这个事件让我觉得，安全边界不能只看“模型有没有训练用户数据”，还要继续追问：客户端读取了什么、上传了什么、谁能够解密、数据保存多久，以及用户是否真的拥有关闭这些功能的能力。

解决方案

Anthropic 在 6 月调整 Claude Fable 的数据政策后，Fable 默认要求保留 30 天数据，用于安全监测（Anthropic, 2026a）。这项变化引发了部分企业对 ZDR（Zero Data Retention，零数据留存）、知识产权和日志保存范围的担忧。

在 9 月 10 日威胁报告披露后的几天内，企业客户对 AI 数据边界的担忧也开始公开化。9 月 14 日，Reuters 援引 The Information 报道，NVIDIA、Palantir、Booz Allen 等公司已经开始限制 Anthropic 模型在敏感工作流中的使用（Reuters, 2026）。

按照数据敏感程度，可以采用不同的解决方案：

理想情况下，所有数据都可以在本地处理，不需要离开设备。哪怕云服务商提供合规审查和零数据留存保证，只要数据离开本地，就已经进入了新的信任边界，不能再按照本地处理的安全等级来对待。

因此，未来的重点可能会同时落在两个方向：更安全、高效的云端计算，以及足够高效的本地模型。

一个面向个人或小团队的本地 AI 示意组合可以是：

  1. 以 Google Gemma 4 作为基础模型；
  2. 使用 NVIDIA DGX Spark 作为小型 AI 工作站。

不过，这只是一个示意组合。真正的企业级部署还需要 IAM、网络隔离、审计、密钥管理、备份和终端安全。

结语

我这次真正观察到的，不是 Agent 一定会“偷”数据，而是：使用云端 Agent 后，文件的安全边界不再只在本地设备，而是扩展到了模型厂商、客户端、代理服务、插件和工具链。

Agent 越强，能够读取和操作的范围就越大；因此，权限最小化、数据分级和可验证的供应链透明度，也会变得越来越重要。

参考文献

Anthropic. (2026b, September 10). Detecting and countering misuse of AI: September 2026. https://www.anthropic.com/threat-intelligence-report-september-2026

Ferstar. (2026, September 18). 某国产大模型厂商静默上传全量 Git 历史的调查 [Investigating a Chinese model provider’s silent upload of the full Git history]. Code is cheap, let’s talk. 原始报道

IT之家. (2026, September 18). 某国产大模型厂商被质疑“偷传代码”：官方回应称问题已修复，将开源代码库、引入第三方审查 [Chinese model provider accused of “stealing code”: Official response says the issue has been fixed and the codebase will be open-sourced]. IT之家. https://www.ithome.com/1/004/310.htm

PDFMathTranslate. (n.d.). PDFMathTranslate [Computer software]. GitHub. https://github.com/PDFMathTranslate/PDFMathTranslate

Hackathon (Hackthon) is a portmanteau combining hacker and marathon.

Originally, it was a competition where skilled programmers gathered together to complete a real programming project from scratch in roughly 24–48 hours, followed by a final evaluation.

Today, as AI has significantly lowered the barrier to making software, more people have entered the software development industry. Hackathons have also become increasingly common in China, and their meaning has changed accordingly.

By the Old school definition of a hackathon, the project must be developed from 0 to 1, and the process often involves staying up late or working through the night.
PS: Once you enter a flow state, you really should not interrupt it lightly, because the rhythm can easily break. At the same time, a fondness for staying up late is also a problem among programmers who are “well-paid, have little work, and die young” (reportedly the best profession for finding a spouse).

Hackathons in China today look more like a “showcase” — glamorous venues, high-resolution DSLR photography, and various sponsors’ resources gathered together. At the final competition, investors and corporate executives recruit through Boss Zhipin.

Of course, neither has an inherent advantage over the other. The former is more “Old School”, more “under ground”, and more “Real”. The latter can bring greater commercial exposure and more peer resources.

Offline Hackathon Experience

I signed up for a hackathon held in Hong Kong at the beginning of March. At the time, I mainly wanted to see what other people were working on.

When I first registered, I carefully evaluated my own project. Most of it had already been completed before the competition, so I was somewhat uneasy about whether I was qualified to enter.

Still, I followed the rules and submitted my project Demo on the organizer’s official website.

As far as I remember, the competition format was roughly: online registration -> preliminary Demo submission -> offline coding in the second round -> second-round presentation.

It lasted two days. The first day included the opening, speeches by the judges, and coding. The second day included coding and presentations.

In practice, the atmosphere did not feel like an especially tense marathon. There was no strict requirement to stay at the venue either. After being cooped up in the room for a long time, I instead felt that the carbon dioxide level was getting high and became sleepy.

I returned to Shenzhen that evening and attended the presentations the next day.

Some photos from the offline competition:



Follow-up and Launch

At that time, the basic functions of the app were complete and it had already been packaged for TestFlight, though it had not yet passed App Store review.

After I demonstrated one recognition on site, the project received the highest number of votes in the group and across the whole event during the audience voting that followed.

Within two months after the presentation, I completed the website development and launched the app on the Apple App Store.

About Hackathons

If I separate out what I truly gained from this hackathon, it was probably:

  1. Learning how to present my project to the public. It was rushed, and even the PPT was generated with Kimi, but presentation was still a key part of promotion.
  2. Meeting peers and seniors who were equally enthusiastic about AI
  3. Learning more about the complexity of the real world

After reading some online articles later, I learned that most hackathons today actually involve entering with an existing product. Some manufacturers even hire contestants to release and introduce their products for promotional purposes. In that sense, they are quite different from Old School hackathons.

Times change, and so does the value between technology and media, development and marketing. Perhaps that is not necessarily a bad thing.

黑客松（Hackthon）是一个组合词，把黑客（Hacker）和Marathon（马拉松）结合在了一起。

最初是编程高手们聚集在一起，在大约24-48小时内从0开始完成一个真实的编程项目的比赛，最终进行评比。

时至今日，随着Ai让制作一个软件的门槛大幅度降低，更多的人参加到了软件开发行业。黑客松在国内也开始举办地越来越多，相应的含义也发生了改变。

按照Old school的黑客松定义，必须是从0-1开发，而且常常伴随着熬夜和通宵。
PS：因为进入心流之后确实不要轻易打断，否则节奏很容易断开，不过喜欢熬夜也确实是程序员群体「钱多事少死的早」的一个问题（据说是最佳择偶对象职业）

而现在国内的黑客松更加像是一个“秀场”——光鲜靓丽的场馆、高清单反摄影、各种赞助商资源聚焦在一起，最终比赛时投资人、企业高管Boss直聘。

当然两者并没有孰优孰劣之分。相比之下，前者更加的“Old School”，更加“under ground”、更加的“Real”。而后者，可以带来更多的商业曝光和同伴资源等。

线下参赛经历

笔者本人在三月初的时候报名参加了在香港举办的黑客松，当时的想法是报名看看其他人在做什么事情。

最初报名的时候仔细评估了一下自己的作品，其实绝大部分在参加比赛之前已经完成了，所以还有些忐忑是否有资格报名。

不过还是按照赛制规则，在举办方的官网上提交了我的作品Demo。

记忆里大致的赛制是这样的：线上报名-初赛提交Demo-复赛线下Coding-复赛路演

一共两天，第一天是开赛、评委演讲还有Coding，第二天是Coding还有路演。

实际体验下来并没有特别紧张的马拉松氛围，也没有规定很死一定要在场地里，反而是由于一直闷在房间里，感觉二氧化碳有些超标，犯困了。

当天晚上返回了深圳，第二天参加路演。

一些线下参赛的照片：



后续与落地

当时这个App的开发进度是基本的功能已经完成，同时已经打包上TestFlight了，但是还没通过AppStore的审核。

我在现场演示了一次识别之后，在后续的观众投票环节获得了小组（也是全场）最高票

而在参加完路演之后的2个月内，我跑通了网站开发和苹果商城上线。

关于黑客松

在这次黑客松上，如果抽丝剥离出我真正的收获的话，大概有：

  1. 学习了如何向大众展示自己的项目，虽然很仓促，甚至PPT都是用Kimi生成的，但是这也是宣发的重点
  2. 认识了同样对AI有热情的同辈、前辈等
  3. 了解到了更多真实社会的复杂性

后续阅读了一些网络文章才知道，原来黑客松在如今其实大部分都是带着产品参赛的，而且还有一些厂家会雇佣选手发布和介绍自己的产品，目的就是为了宣传。可以说是和Old School的黑客松大相径庭。

不过时代在变化，技术和媒体、开发和营销之间价值也在变化，或许这也不是一件坏事吧。

When I first built this personal website, I wanted to buy a domain, but I did not know much about domain providers at the time.

At that point, I had not yet learned about a workflow such as “GPT searches for the best practices in an industry, then chooses one to put into practice.”

So I explored the internet freely, read various blog posts, and even visited abc.xyz, the website purchased by Google co-founder Larry Page.

(My first impression of the .xyz domain was that it felt very unreliable, with an intuition that it might belong to some questionable industry. Later, after discussing it with Gemini, I learned that .xyz was also one of the early internet domain extensions. Larry Page buying this website also had the bold feeling of a wealthy person buying a license plate number like 8888.)

Returning to the main topic, the more established domain-purchase websites I identified were

Cloudflare https://www.cloudflare.com/domains/search

Spaceship https://www.spaceship.com/zh/

For people who are unfamiliar with this knowledge, a .com domain is generally the most reliable choice. Since caoyueyang.com had already been registered in 2016, I chose the .org extension instead (at least it would not be mistaken for a strange website).

The price of a domain includes:

  • Registry cost: the fee charged by the operator of the domain extension; this is the underlying cost.
  • Registrar markup: Cloudflare, Namecheap, GoDaddy, Porkbun, and similar companies add some profit to the cost.
  • ICANN fee: some generic domains have a small ICANN fee, usually around $0.18/year.
  • Taxes: depending on your billing address, this may include VAT, GST, or Sales Tax.
  • Payment and exchange-rate costs: if you pay in U.S. dollars with a credit card denominated in RMB, HKD, or JPY, your bank may charge a foreign-exchange fee.
  • WHOIS Privacy: many registrars provide it for free, while some may still charge for it.
  • First-year promotion versus renewal price: this is the easiest trap. The first year might cost $0.99, while the second year could become $20+.

Therefore, most domains can be found in the price range of 5–20 U.S. dollars, and domain prices are also affected by supply and demand.

For example, the .ai extension was originally a country-code top-level domain (ccTLD) representing Anguilla, a British overseas territory in the Caribbean. Due to the popularity of artificial intelligence, prices have risen considerably, as the images show. Domain choices should therefore follow the actual situation and budget.

Tips

A domain can be purchased for up to 10 years at a time. If it expires without renewal, someone else may register it, so remember to renew it on time.

I had wanted to build an app that could quickly and automatically review contracts and provide suggestions. Yesterday, I officially started working on it.

Before starting, I thought about several questions:

  1. Why are large language models suitable for language review?
  2. Since general-purpose AI products such as ChatGPT already exist, why build an app or Agent ourselves?
    I will organize these thoughts one by one.

Why Are Large Language Models Suitable for Language Review?

Not long ago, I applied for an RA position at HKU and made a small demo for reviewing IFC models in BIM.
The product demo is available at: https://bim-review-agent.andycaoyy6.chatgpt.site/
PS: Since the website is hosted by ChatGPT, please use an IP address that can access ChatGPT services.

In my experience, most people’s feelings toward AI are now shifting from excitement to emptiness.

The “bosses” who control resources think AI can improve efficiency. Then why should I hire so many employees? If AI can do it, why can’t you? How can I accelerate my digital transformation?
To most bosses, FDE (Foward Deployed Engineering) has effectively become the role of an “operations supervisor”, with the only metric being: “How many people can I lay off?”

Employees who possess knowledge and skills, on the other hand, worry that if AI learns all of their knowledge and skills, how can they protect their own interests? Will this ultimately become a case of “teaching one’s apprentice and starving oneself”?
References:

  1. https://www.qbitai.com/2026/04/402063.html
  2. https://medium.com/@kanishks772/meta-allegedly-used-employee-workflows-to-train-ai-then-laid-off-8-000-people-b267da7a63ec

Moreover, whenever someone says, “My XXXX was completed with the help of AI,”

people tend to think it is “a rough and poorly made product” rather than “a cool, high-tech, high-value product.”

Although the scope and applications of AI (Artificial Intelligence) extend far beyond natural language processing, it is certainly one of the applications that currently affects our lives the most.

Therefore, I believe a good AI product or application should make people unaware of the AI inside it, while producing results that are verifiable, accurate, and highly precise.

Legal contracts are standardized documents that require rigorous logic and language, with standard formats available for comparison. NLP (Natural Language Processing) happens to be one of the areas where large language models are relatively strong.

Therefore, handing a problem or image to a large language model for screening, highlighting problematic areas, providing references, and finally returning feedback creates a good closed loop. It is also an area where AI can provide significant acceleration.

Most importantly, I personally encounter many situations involving employment contracts, rental contracts, civil contracts, and commercial contracts. One purpose of building this product is to create an efficient solution for myself.

Vertical Agents and General-Purpose Agents

The next question is: since general-purpose apps such as ChatGPT, Doubao, and Gemini already exist, what is the point of developing such a product?

In the past, when I encountered a problem, my usual process was to upload the document to GPT, ask GPT to review it, obtain feedback through repeated questions, and sometimes even generate a new PDF directly.

This question is not limited to app development. It can apply to almost any field: if there is already a powerful and lower-cost solution, why build one ourselves?

Here is a comparison:
Develop it ourselves:

  1. Greater freedom in choosing data-processing solutions
  2. Freedom to choose data-storage solutions
  3. There is a gap between our model and Agent capabilities

Give the data to a major provider:

  1. Faster response
  2. Fixed and non-customizable workflows
  3. All data must be handed over to the provider’s servers

It is clear that the advantages and disadvantages of developing independently are both significant. The advantages are greater freedom, more selective disclosure of data, and better integration with existing workflows.

The disadvantage is that processing efficiency still falls behind the major providers’ models. If we ultimately still use a model provider’s API, the scope of data confidentiality remains limited.

So this is a trade-off between security and efficiency.

It can also be described as centralization versus decentralization, Leviathan versus Behemoth…

Development Process

First, I researched “industry best practices” and asked CodeX/GPT to conduct industry research.

I then referred to related apps and designs, testing their functions through Computer Use or by connecting to mobile apps through developer mode, while also drawing on their design approaches.

Obtaining a Design Draft with Figma Make

I then asked CodeX to read the entire folder and provide a prompt for Figma Make, Figma’s built-in AI design feature, to create an initial MVP design.

Save the design draft as a Figma file. (For steps you do not know how to complete, Computer Use can be used as a fallback.)

Next, connect Figma and CodeX through an MCP server and let Figma automatically develop the frontend UI.
Reference: https://help.figma.com/hc/en-us/articles/39888629089175-Codex-and-Figma-Set-up-the-MCP-server

During this process, I can discuss long-term storage and system-architecture choices with CodeX and save them in the repository as an Agent.md file or a specification document.

Logo and Visual Design

For the visual design, I also discussed the logo with GPT.
To represent legal fairness and impartiality, I used the scales of justice, one of the most common legal symbols, as the visual center.
I also added elements of the judge character, Dragonfly Captain, from the Japanese tokusatsu series B-Robo Kabutack.

Build and Testing

Once development is complete, I can test stability and reliability on different emulators or real devices.

As for release, promotion, commercialization, and continuous iteration, that is another matter.

Summary

Overall, this is a loop of AI drafting -> refinement based on personalized aesthetics -> continuous iteration based on personal and market feedback.

Preview

This is a preview of the current Android version. Please stay tuned for the finished product.

之前一直想要做一个APP，能够帮我快速自动审查合同并且给出建议，所以昨天正式开始做这一件事情

在做这个事情之前思考了几个问题：

  1. 大语言模型为什么适合做语言审查？
  2. 既然已经有通用的人工智能产品ChatGPT了，为什么还要自己制作一个APP/Agent？
    挨个整理一下思绪。

大语言模型为什么适合做语言审查？

在不久之前投递了HKU的RA岗位，做了一个小的Demo，做的事情就是BIM里面的IFC模型审查
产品Demo可以通过网址：https://bim-review-agent.andycaoyy6.chatgpt.site/ 访问
PS:由于使用的是ChatGPT提供的网站托管服务，所以请使用支持Chatgpt服务的IP访问

实际上，依据我的个人经验，现在多数人对于AI对感觉，从兴奋开始转向虚无。

掌握资源的“老板”们觉得AI可以帮助我提效，那么为什么我还要雇佣这么多雇员？AI可以做到为什么你做不到？我怎么加速我的数字化转型？
FDE（Foward Deployed Engineering）在大多数的老板眼里，实际上已经是“东西厂主管”的角色，唯一负责的指标是“我可以裁多少人？”

而掌握知识技能的雇员们认为，如果我的知识技能都被AI学习走了，那么我自己的利益怎么保护？最终难道不会”教会徒弟饿死师傅“吗？
参考链接：

  1. https://www.qbitai.com/2026/04/402063.html
  2. https://medium.com/@kanishks772/meta-allegedly-used-employee-workflows-to-train-ai-then-laid-off-8-000-people-b267da7a63ec

而且目前一旦提到，“我的XXXX是在AI帮助下完成的”。

在我看来，人们的认知里面只会觉得“这是一个粗制滥造的东西”，而不是“这是一个非常高科技含量的很酷的、很有含金量的东西”。

虽然AI（Artificial Intelligence）的范围和应用远不止是自然语言处理，但是确实它是目前影响我们生活最多的一个应用。

所以，我认为，一个好的AI产品/应用，应该让人察觉不到AI在其中，而且结果是可以验证的、准确的、高精度的。

法律合同这样的标准文书写作需要对逻辑和语言非常严谨，并且有标准样式可以参考对比，NLP（Natural Language Processing）恰好就是大语言模型比较擅长的地方。

因此，把问题/图像交给大语言模型做筛查，接着将有问题的地方进行高亮，并且给出参考文献，最终给出反馈意见，就是一个很好的闭环，也是可以用AI可以极大加速的地方。

当然最主要的是，我自己个人会遇到很多诸如劳动合同、租房合同、民事商务合同等的情况，所以做这个产品的一个目的之一，也是我自己希望有一个高效的解决方案。

垂直Agent和通用Agent

接着问题又来了——既然已经有ChatGPT/豆包/Gemini这样的通用APP，开发这样的一个产品的意义何在？

在过去我遇到问题的时候，大多数的流程是：将文件内容上传给GPT，接着让GPT给我审查，通过反复提问得到反馈，甚至直接生成新的PDF。

这个问题其实不仅限于APP开发，几乎可以套用到任何领域：既然已经有一个非常强大的更低成本的解决方案，为什么还要自己做？

对比一下两者的区别：
自己开发：

  1. 更加高自由度的数据处理方案选择
  2. 自由选择数据存储方案
  3. 模型能力和Agent能力存在差距

将数据给巨头：

  1. 更快速的响应
  2. 工作流程固定化，不可定制
  3. 数据需要全部交给巨头的服务器

所以可以看出，自己开发的好处和坏处都很明显，好处就是更多的自由度，并且可以将数据更加有选择性地披露，同时可以更好地与当前的工作流结合。

坏处就是，在处理效率上，依然和巨头的模型有差距，而且如果最终还是要使用模型供应商的API，那么最终数据保密的范围依然只能是有限度的。

所以这是一个 安全VS效率的 Trade off

也可以说是，中心化VS去中心化，利维坦VS贝希摩斯……

开发流程

首先进行“行业最佳实践”调研，让CodeX/GPT进行行业最佳调研

接着对相关的APP和设计进行参考，例如通过Computer Use或者通过开发者模式连接手机APP，对功能进行测试，并且对设计思路进行参考。

通过FigmaMake获取设计稿

接着让CodeX阅读整个文件夹内容，给出发送给FigmaMake（设计软件Figma自带的AI设计功能）进行初版的MVP设计。

将设计稿内容保存为Figma文件（所有不会的步骤可以考虑用Computer Use进行兜底辅助）

后续将Figma和CodeX通过MCP服务器连接，让Figma全自动进行前端UI开发
参考链接：https://help.figma.com/hc/en-us/articles/39888629089175-Codex-and-Figma-Set-up-the-MCP-server

在此期间可以和CodeX讨论如何做长期存储、系统架构方案选择等，保存到仓库里作为Agent.md或者Spec文档等。

Logo和视觉

在视觉设计上，也是和GPT讨论了Logo怎么设计。
为了体现法律公平公正，所以采用了法律最常用的天平作为视觉中心。
而且还加入了日本特摄剧《铁甲小宝》里面的裁判——蜻蜓队长的元素。

Build和测试

当开发完成后就可以自己在不同模拟器或者真实设备上测试稳定性，可靠性等了。

至于发布和推广商业化和持续迭代优化，那又是另一回事了

总结

总的来看，这是一个AI打草稿->依据个性化审美优化->根据自己和市场的反馈不断迭代的Loop
